section_summary: This section is dominated by U.S. diplomatic reporting on Japanese communities and alleged Axis activity in Peru, including a detailed Embassy survey of settlements in southern Peru and a broader recommendation to deport or relocate Peru’s Japanese population. It also documents Chinese cooperation with American investigators, intercepted Japanese correspondence, suspected propaganda operations involving Chilean journalists returning from Japan, and proposed controls on Japanese schools, radios, travel, and residence near strategic coastal areas. Additional records include cross-reference sheets, intelligence-distribution notices, routing papers, duplicate file copies, and reports concerning Colombia, Chile, Brazil, and the exchange ship Gripsholm.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: conference between the Japanese ambassadors to Argentina and Chile
subfiles.about: References a telegram concerning confidential information about a possible meeting between the Japanese ambassadors in Argentina and Chile.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 707: a reported conference between the Japanese ambassadors to Argentina and Chile, requested to be investigated.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: investigation of alleged Japanese ambassadorial conference
subfiles.about: References a telegram reporting no reason to believe that the Japanese ambassador in Santiago met the Japanese ambassador to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The cross-reference identifies telegram no. 1029 from Chile. It records the negative result of an investigation into the reported conference.

subfiles.title: Departmental summary of despatch no. 4138 on Japanese activities in southern Peru
subfiles.about: Summarizes an American-Chinese survey of Japanese establishments and activities in southern Peru.
subfiles.summary: Summary of Despatch No. 4138: Emmerson and a Chinese Legation representative visited southern Peru; Arequipa's small Japanese community is influential and Okinawans separate; Chinese contacts will keep reporting.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 4138: Investigation of Japanese Activities in Southern Peru
subfiles.doc_type: despatch with memorandum and six enclosures
subfiles.about: Reports an Embassy-Chinese Legation tour investigating Japanese communities in Arequipa, Nasca, Ica, Pisco, Cañete and Chincha Alta.
subfiles.summary: Patterson forwards Emmerson and George Tsung-Yuan Woo’s account of a week-long investigative journey through southern Peru, where Chinese associations supplied names, photographs and observations about Japanese residents. The enclosures describe population estimates, businesses, schools, associations, travel, fishing, hunting, alleged military affiliations, possible clandestine radio activity and strategic coastal locations. The investigators considered Arequipa’s prosperous Japanese merchants and the large Cañete Valley community particularly significant, while viewing Nasca’s small community as relatively unimportant. The report repeatedly notes weak local enforcement and the willingness of Chinese community leaders to continue gathering information.

subfiles.title: Distribution notice for despatch no. 4138
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Distributes the Lima Embassy’s report on Japanese activities in southern Peru to U.S. intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: Distribution notice for Despatch No. 4138 to military, naval and federal intelligence.

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a confidential telegram on a reported conference between Japanese ambassadors, to be investigated and verified.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary duplicate of despatch no. 422: Harmful Effect of United Press Despatches
subfiles.about: Introduces an anonymous complaint that United Press reporting in Colombia favored Axis war communiqués.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate first-page fragment of Despatch No. 422: a Popayan correspondent objects to US news service dissemination of German and Japanese war claims.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 422: Harmful Effect of United Press Despatches, file copy
subfiles.about: Forwards an anonymous Colombian complaint about allegedly pro-Axis United Press war coverage.
subfiles.summary: Keith quotes a July 4 letter from Popayán asserting that United Press emphasized bulletins from Berlin, Rome and Tokyo and thereby harmed the Allied cause. Although anonymous, the Embassy considered the letter confirmation of concerns it had already raised about the influence of such reporting in Colombia.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 422: Harmful Effect of United Press Despatches, true copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Bogotá Embassy report on the alleged propaganda effects of United Press dispatches.
subfiles.summary: This true copy repeats the anonymous Popayán letter accusing United Press of presenting Axis broadcasts favorably and Allied policy negatively. Keith again argues that the anonymous character of the complaint does little to reduce its significance.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: fishing facilities at Iquitos and Talara
subfiles.about: References despatch no. 3381 containing information about fishing facilities at Iquitos and Talara.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs researchers to a separately filed Peruvian despatch. It links the fishing-facilities information to the Japanese-activities subject file.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 113 ordering a covert search of Rosero’s effects
subfiles.to: American consul, Lourenço Marques, for Commander H. H. Smith-Hutton
subfiles.about: Orders a secret search for Japanese war films and negatives allegedly carried by Chilean consul Jorge Rosero aboard the Asama Maru and Gripsholm.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 113: Rosero traveling from Yokohama to Lima with secret war pictures and negatives; Smith-Hutton to covertly search his effects and secure seized material in the Gripsholm captain's safe, with ONI concurring.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 2974 reporting the search of Rosero’s effects
subfiles.from: Simmons, Rio de Janeiro, relaying Lieutenant Commander Smith-Hutton
subfiles.about: Reports that the covert search ordered at Lourenço Marques found three rolls of Leica negatives but no photographs.
subfiles.summary: Smith-Hutton reports the search was completed, finding three rolls of Leica negatives.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of forwarded Chinese diplomatic covers
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of two covers from Chinese diplomatic offices in Panama and Managua.
subfiles.summary: The secretary, for Dr. Soong, thanks Hamilton for forwarding items, expressing Chinese appreciation.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 4477: Cooperation by the Chinese Legation, file copy
subfiles.about: Recommends formally thanking the Chinese government for its Legation’s assistance in investigating Japanese activities in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 4477 (file copy): the Embassy praises the Chinese Minister's cooperation and George Woo's extensive travel and investigative work with American officers.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 4477: Cooperation by the Chinese Legation, signed copy
subfiles.from: R. Henry Norweb, American Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Requests an expression of appreciation for Chinese Legation assistance to the American Embassy in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 4477 (signed): Norweb says the Chinese Minister made Legation resources available to American investigators, crediting George Woo's fieldwork and language skills.

subfiles.title: Distribution notice for despatch no. 4477
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Distributes the Lima Embassy’s despatch praising Chinese Legation cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Distribution notice for Despatch No. 4477 to US intelligence agencies.

subfiles.title: London telegram no. 4016 on Chilean reporters and Japanese propaganda
subfiles.from: John G. Winant, American Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Reports British intelligence that Japan intended to use returning Chilean reporters for propaganda and intelligence purposes.
subfiles.summary: London telegram: British sources allege Jorge Rosero carried six Japanese war-news films and would gather intelligence in Peru; Aburto carried industrial films; both traveled on the Asama Maru.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase to Santiago of London telegram on Rosero and Aburto
subfiles.about: Passes to Santiago the British-source allegations concerning Rosero, Aburto and Japanese use of Chilean journalists.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase to Santiago of London's report on Rosero and Aburto carrying Japanese films aboard the Asama Maru.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: memorandum on the Japanese problem in Peru
subfiles.from: Department of State, Foreign Activity Correlation (Hanley)
subfiles.about: References a memorandum discussing the Japanese population in Peru and possible internment in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a Pacific War memorandum on interning Japanese nationals from Peru in the United States.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 3437 seeking identification of a Chilean deputy
subfiles.about: Asks whether Chilean deputy Rafael Moreno, or a similarly named deputy, visited Rio de Janeiro in late August.
subfiles.summary: Telegram seeks identification of a Chilean deputy named in earlier telegrams and confirmation of his presence in Rio.

subfiles.title: Charge slip associated with the Japanese-problem records
subfiles.about: Records later administrative circulation of an enclosure in the 894.20210 file.
subfiles.summary: The page consists principally of handwritten charge and routing entries. Most names and references are too unclear to identify reliably.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 4618: The Japanese Problem in Peru—Review and Recommendation
subfiles.from: R. Henry Norweb, American Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Reviews the Japanese population in Peru and recommends mass removal, deportation of leaders, coastal exclusions and other security controls.
subfiles.summary: Norweb estimates that roughly 25,000 people of Japanese ancestry lived in Peru, heavily concentrated around Lima and Callao, and describes Embassy efforts to compile intelligence through American agencies and Chinese informants. He argues that earlier deportations were undermined by political influence, bribery and substitution of volunteers for people whom the Embassy considered dangerous. The despatch presents removal to U.S. relocation centers as the preferred permanent solution and recommends immediate expulsion of community leaders, removal from strategic coastal areas, inland relocation, closure of schools, special policing, prohibition of short-wave radios and counterpropaganda broadcasts. It also acknowledges legal, shipping and administrative obstacles to mass removal.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on weak Peruvian control of Axis activity
subfiles.from: Baldwin, Division of the American Republics
subfiles.about: Criticizes Peruvian enforcement against Axis movement and activity as described in Lima despatch no. 4467.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites clandestine radios, police bribery, unauthorized entry into Talara, Japanese-language teaching, Proclaimed List violations and transfers of energetic police officers. Baldwin calls the situation lamentable and asks whether new instructions to Lima or discussions with Peruvian representatives might improve it. Pages 57–58 are attached routing and division sheets.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs routing memorandum on despatch no. 4618
subfiles.about: Calls attention to the American Republics Division’s summary of Lima despatch no. 4618.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum states that the underlying despatch on the Japanese problem in Peru is well summarized by the attached American Republics memorandum. It recommends that colleagues read that summary; page 60 contains its routing list.

subfiles.title: Summary of Lima despatch no. 4618
subfiles.about: Summarizes Norweb’s estimate of Peru’s Japanese population and his eight recommended control measures.
subfiles.summary: Summary of Lima Despatch No. 4618: about 25,000 persons of Japanese ancestry in Peru; controls ineffective despite about 500 deportations; mass removal impracticable; lists proposed expulsions, relocation, school closures and radio ban.

subfiles.title: Duplicate summary of Lima despatch no. 4618
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Department’s summary of the Embassy’s review and recommendations concerning Japanese residents in Peru.
subfiles.summary: This copy again states that Japanese movement, schools and associations remained inadequately controlled and that a mass removal program was the Embassy’s preferred solution. It reproduces the same eight recommendations for deportation, relocation, coastal security, policing, radio restrictions and propaganda.

subfiles.title: Distribution notice for despatch no. 4618
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Distributes the Lima Embassy’s review and recommendations concerning the Japanese problem in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Distribution notice for Despatch No. 4618 to US intelligence agencies.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on Chilean journalists returning from Japan
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Reports an unconfirmed allegation that returning Chilean journalist Iglesias and his wife were anti-American and possible Japanese agents.
subfiles.summary: FBI: Chilean journalists returning from Japan will pass through the US; the Santiago Embassy regretted they were not going to Buenos Aires first; unconfirmed allegation against Iglesias and wife.

subfiles.title: Instruction no. 2084 to Santiago on Iglesias and returning journalists
subfiles.about: Quotes the FBI report about Iglesias and other Chilean journalists for the Embassy’s confidential information and possible comment.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 2084 repeats the Santiago Embassy's disappointment over the journalists' route and the unverified claim that Iglesias and wife were possible agents.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum on priorities for handling the Japanese problem in Peru
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations, Navy Department
subfiles.to: Orme Wilson, State Department liaison officer
subfiles.about: Endorses Norweb’s recommendations and identifies four measures as immediate national-security priorities.
subfiles.summary: Navy supports the Lima Embassy proposals, prioritizing removing Japanese from coastal areas, banning short-wave radios, closing Japanese schools and assigning special police.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 4850: Translation of an intercepted communication from a Japanese resident of Trujillo
subfiles.from: R. Henry Norweb, American Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Forwards and analyzes a pro-Japanese letter intercepted between Japanese residents of Trujillo and Lima.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 4850: an intercepted Trujillo letter to two Japanese the Embassy recommended expelling condemns Peruvian investigations, expects Axis victory and blames the US for Peru's economic difficulties.

subfiles.title: Distribution notice for despatch no. 4850
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Distributes the intercepted Trujillo communication and the Lima Embassy’s analysis to U.S. intelligence agencies.
subfiles.summary: Distribution notice for Despatch No. 4850 and its intercepted Trujillo communication.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum quoting the Japanese Embassy’s plan for returning Chilean journalists, file copy
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Quotes an intercepted Japanese Embassy message proposing to meet Chilean journalists returning through Rio de Janeiro and Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: FBI quotes the Japanese Embassy's fear that Americans would turn returning Chilean journalists against Japan; it proposes sending Yatoi and Miyazaki to Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: FBI memorandum on the Japanese Embassy plan for returning Chilean journalists, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Duplicates the confidential-source report of an August 5 message from the Japanese Embassy in Santiago to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate FBI memo: Yatoi and Miyazaki to meet the journalists, returning on the Gripsholm, in Buenos Aires before American officials could influence them.

subfiles.title: Instruction no. 2155 to Santiago on the Japanese Embassy message
subfiles.about: Passes the intercepted Japanese Embassy message about efforts to influence returning Chilean journalists to the Embassy in Santiago.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 2155 quotes the plan to send Yatoi and Miyazaki to Buenos Aires for Chilean journalists returning via Rio.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: organization of Japanese colonies in Latin America
subfiles.about: References a Panama despatch transmitting a memorandum on the organization of Japanese communities in Latin America.
subfiles.summary: The sheet points to despatch no. 2989 in file 894.20232/106. It links that memorandum to the present Japanese-activities file.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: return of Chilean journalists from Japan
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of the American Republics (Baldwin)
subfiles.about: References a memorandum commenting on the return of Chilean journalists from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to file 825.91294/5 on the return of Chilean journalists from Japan.
